A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic overlap simulations in Figure 1 and model-training evaluations of predicted mixtures and cross-scale extrapolation in Sections 5.3–5.4 and Figures 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic simulations and model-training results, including the appendix Pile-CC evaluation in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The Extended Quantization Model, Extended Linear Regression Model, capacity-allocation objective, and mixture-optimization algorithm remain unchanged. Writing losses as L(h|N,D) instead of L(h,N,D) does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 17-domain Pile, four-domain, seven-domain SlimPajama, and synthetic tail-overlap evaluations, including the same cross-scale extrapolation scenarios.

E2.justification: The Additive, Exponential, BiMix, and RegMix comparisons in Table 2 and Figure 2 are unchanged, as are the uniform-mixture and extrapolation comparators. The newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Splits, model scales, token budgets, fitting procedures, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Section 5 now explicitly calls MRE and MAE domain-averaged; MRE averaging was already specified in Section 5.2. This and the overlap-caption addition disclose details rather than establish changed protocols.

E4.justification: Figure 1 retains the same noisy and noiseless robustness test at 20%, 30%, and 40% tail overlap. Its expanded caption explains the existing simulation; no ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. The empirical comparisons retain the same point estimates, without added repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 still reports 1.533% MRE and 0.034 MAE for the Eq. (3) model. All results and rankings in Figures 1–5, including the appendix Pile-CC curves, are retained without numerical updates or added result entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, bounds, and proofs remain unchanged, including Appendices D–E. The loss-notation changes in Theorems 4.1 and D.19 and the switch from 'Given' to 'For any' mixture restate the existing formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1 contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about capacity competition, data-dependent noise, fitting accuracy, optimal mixtures, cross-scale extrapolation, and parameter efficiency.

C2.justification: The explanations of capacity competition, noise-driven mixture shifts, and overlap robustness are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning unseen domains and downstream tasks, explicit overlap modeling, and non-convex parameter fitting.

D1.justification: Figure 1 newly explains that tail skills are randomly selected for sharing, with each skill overlapping with probability p. Section 5 also clarifies metric aggregation. These are limited documentation additions; Appendix C, Table 4, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Hamidieh et al. (2025) on domain interactions and data synergy, and Medvedev et al. (2025) on mismatched training proportions improving test performance. These modestly broaden the related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand related work, clarify metric wording, and express loss dependence using conditional notation that emphasizes fixed model and data scales. The section order, overall narrative, and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives a longer explanatory caption, and added text causes limited paragraph and bibliography reflow. The plots, table structures, axes, legends, and figure/table inventory remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and contextualization: Figure 1 explains how overlap is generated, Section 5 clarifies metric averaging, and Section 2 acknowledges two relevant prior studies. These are useful documentation gains, while the methods, proofs, and empirical support remain unchanged.
